title: [Lean] Connect reference SCALE traversal to exact dyadic arithmetic
body:
## Summary

Publish four unchanged independently kernel-checked modules connecting scalar Hosting realization, explicit flat reference traversal and exact dyadic SCALE/addition. The new sources total 28,617 bytes, with 27 accepted axiom probes and four full printed types. Seven existing public/import-derived modules are pinned and reconstructed separately; the complete research closure is 11 modules / 79,813 bytes.

## Author-checked scientific context

κ = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918, for the pinned PR1094 context. Both source authors checked this value and scope. This package neither changes κ nor proves the full selected-κ multiplication theorem.

## Coverage and limits

Finite/source-bound coverage: the selected row-one SCALE application and the explicit flat component traversal. Parameterized reference coverage: chart-independent scalar action, all-prefix integer/exponent decoding, exact mixed-exponent addition and numerator magnitude budget. Full-theorem coverage: the selected physical runtime, bit-cost recurrence and multiplication theorem are still open. Dirty accumulator behavior and supplied Hosting/traversal premises remain explicit. There is no finite-word initialization, physical allocation, scratch restoration or selected global rounding/precision supplier in this chunk.

## Acceptance and attribution

See the public source-bound acceptance summary and immutable reproduction recipe. Historical preparation comments are preserved; the exact source hashes bind their later successful acceptance. No new proof replay was used for publication. Reuse PR1802 and PR1985, the credited DreamingOfClouds PR509/516 LemmaG/LemmaA work, and Gareth Davidson/bitplane PR1309 PrefixNorm with its original header and import-only adaptation. James Chang with OpenAI assistance, Apache-2.0.

## Exact adoption

Publication parent: 1ff5f7bc448445516944f10c8e7834db371103aa. The five selected-result, assembly, selected-source and emitter blobs match the previously checked context exactly; contextual kappa is unchanged. No accepted proof was rerun for this adoption.
